div.head: Ine 37
div.ab: LXXXI. Se ciorlisca mon, þe oft betogen wære þifðe, ⁊ ðonne æt siðestan cyrre synnigne mon gefó in ceace oþþe æt openre scylde elles, slea him mon hond oððe fot.
LXXXI. Se cirlisca mon, se ðe oft betygen wære ðiefðe, ⁊ þonne æt siðestan synnigne gefó in ceace oððe elles æt openre scylde, slea him mon hond óf oððe fót.
Cirliscus homo, qui fuerit sepe inculpatus de furto et tunc postea culpabilis inuentus in captali uel in aliter manifesto reus, amputetur ei manus uel pes.
{LXXXI} Se cirlesca mon se ðe oft betygen wære ðiefðe, ⁊ þonne æt siðestan synnigne gefó in ceape oððe elles æt openre scylde: slea him mon hond óf oððe fót.
A man of the rank of ceorl, who has often been accused of theft, and finally, then, is openly caught either with the goods or in the unlawful act: let his hand or foot be struck off.
If a commoner has often been accused of theft and is at last proved guilty, either in the ordeal or by being caught in the act of committing an offence, his hand or foot shall be struck off.
The ceorl, who has often been accused of theft, and then at last is proved guilty at the ordeal or else in obvious guilt, is to have hand or foot struck off.

Der gemeinfreie Mann, welcher mehrmals des Diebstahls angeklagt worden war: und [wenn man ihn] dann zuletzt als Schuldigen abfasst im Kessel[fang] oder sonst bei offener Schuld, so schlage man ihm Hand oder Fuss ab.
The common freeman who had several times been accused of theft: and [if he is] then at last caught guilty in the cauldron[-ordeal] or otherwise in manifest guilt, let his hand or foot be struck off.
